requirements.text: The parser reads Markdown from standard input and writes HTML to standard output.

requirements.name: parse-block-structure
requirements.text: Blocks: paragraphs, thematic breaks, ATX headings, setext headings, indented code, fenced code, HTML blocks, link reference definitions, block quotes, then lists — lists are the hardest block construct, with lazy continuation, nesting, and tightness.

requirements.name: parse-inline-contents
requirements.text: Inlines: backslash escapes, entity and numeric references, code spans, emphasis and strong emphasis (the delimiter-run algorithm), links and images, autolinks, raw HTML, hard breaks.

requirements.name: provide-stdio-interface
requirements.text:
The deliverable is an executable named commonmark that reads UTF-8 Markdown on stdin
and writes HTML to stdout.

requirements.name: pass-complete-commonmark-suite
requirements.text:
The suite runs unfiltered: no --pattern, no --number, no selector of any kind. spec_tests.py
exits with failed + errored, so exit 0 means the complete CommonMark 0.31.2 suite passed.

requirements.text:
Multiple inner whitespaces are collapsed to a single space (except
in pre tags):

requirements.name: remove-block-whitespace
requirements.text: Whitespace surrounding block-level tags is removed.

requirements.name: normalize-self-closing-tags
requirements.text: Self-closing tags are converted to open tags.

requirements.name: normalize-attributes
requirements.text: Attributes are sorted and lowercased.

requirements.name: convert-references
requirements.text:
References are converted to unicode, except that '<', '>', '&', and
'"' are rendered using entities.

requirements.name: preserve-cdata
requirements.text:
We work around HTMLParser's limitations parsing CDATA
by breaking the input into chunks and passing CDATA chunks
through verbatim.

requirements.name: return-original-on-error
requirements.text: return html  # on error, return unnormalized HTML

requirements.name: parse-link-reference-definitions
requirements.text: A link reference definition consists of a link label, optionally preceded by up to three spaces of indentation, followed by a colon (`:`), optional spaces or tabs (including up to one line ending), a link destination, optional spaces or tabs (including up to one line ending), and an optional link title, which if it is present must be separated from the link destination by spaces or tabs.

requirements.text: There are two basic kinds of links in Markdown. In inline links the destination and title are given immediately after the link text. In reference links the destination and title are defined elsewhere in the document.
